name: Ford & Roman, 'Restrictions on Negative Energy Density in Flat Spacetime' (gr-qc/9607003; PRD 55, 2082 (1997)): Lorentzian-sampled QI for the free massless scalar, rho-hat >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), plus the Sec. 4 curved-spacetime scope remark

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/9607003v2 (submitted 1 Jul 1996, revised 2 Oct 1996, v2 24 Jan 1997), L.H. Ford and T.A. Roman, Tufts; journal ref PRD 55, 2082-2089 (Feb 1997) as cited in Kontou-Sanders arXiv:2003.01815 ref. [74]
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on gr-qc/9607003 returned all 17 pages (abstract, Secs. 1-4, Appendices A-B, references); every quotation below is from that page text; RE-READ in full in a second session (all 17 pages again), every quotation re-checked. Note: Eq.(1) is quoted on p.2 from Ref.[21] (Ford-Roman PRD 51, 4277 (1995)), where it was first derived; this paper re-derives it as Eq.(17), the m -> 0 limit of Eq.(16), by a plane-wave method.

published_statement: p.2 Eq.(1) (and p.5 Eq.(17), the m->0 limit of Eq.(16)): 'for the free quantized massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, rho-hat == (t0/pi) INT_{-oo}^{oo} <T00> dt/(t^2+t0^2) >= -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4), for all choices of the sampling time, t0. Here <T00> is the renormalized expectation value of the energy density evaluated in an arbitrary quantum state |psi>, in the frame of an arbitrary inertial observer whose proper time coordinate is t.' (units hbar = c = 1; the paper's text layer prints 't0' for the proper-time coordinate, an extraction artefact). p.4: 'the energy density is evaluated in the reference frame of an inertial observer, at an arbitrary spatial point which we choose to be x = 0.' Companion results in the same paper: massive scalar rho-hat >= -3 G(y)/(32 pi^2 t0^4), y = 2 m t0 (Eq.16); EM field -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) (Eq.48); 2D massless -1/(8 pi t0^2) (Eq.25). Sec.4 (p.11), the scope remark: 'in Minkowski spacetime, our bounds hold for an arbitrary choice of the sampling time, t0. Recently we ARGUED that such bounds should also hold in a curved spacetime and/or one with boundaries, if the sampling time is restricted to be much smaller than the smallest local radius of curvature and/or the distance to any boundaries in the spacetime [23]. An explicit example ... [24] ... static closed and open Robertson-Walker universe models.' p.2 also: 'In quantum field theory ... the energy density may be unboundedly negative at a spacetime point.'
published_hypotheses: H1 free (non-interacting) quantized field; stress tensor T_mn = phi,m phi,n - (1/2) eta_mn (phi,a phi^,a + m^2 phi^2) (Eq.6) -- MINIMAL coupling (no xi R phi^2 term)
H2 massless scalar for Eq.(1) (massive: Eq.16 with G(y) <= 1; EM: Eq.48, twice as negative)
H3 four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, no boundaries ('derived for Minkowski spacetime, in the absence of boundaries', p.2)

H4 the quantity bounded is the Lorentzian TIME average rho-hat of <T00> along the worldline of an INERTIAL observer at ONE spatial point x = 0, weight t0/[pi(t^2+t0^2)] with unit integral (Eq.8); not <T00> at a point, not a spatial or spacetime average
H5 one-sided: a LOWER bound on rho-hat; nothing bounds positive energy density
H6 arbitrary state |psi> of the Fock space, <T00> renormalized (normal ordered w.r.t. the Minkowski vacuum); the mode sums are assumed convergent in the V -> oo / omega_max -> oo limit (p.16)

H7 holds for ALL t0 > 0 in flat space; the extension to curved spacetime / boundaries for t0 << smallest local curvature radius and/or boundary distance is ARGUED in ref.[23] (PRD 53, 5496), not proved in this paper. The paper names TWO supporting cases: p.2-3 'we proved that the inequality Eq.(1) holds in the case of the Casimir effect for sampling times much smaller than the distance between the plates' (in [23]), and p.3/p.11 the static closed and open Robertson-Walker QIs of ref.[24] (gr-qc/9608005), which reduce to Eq.(1) for short sampling times
H8 the derivation uses no time-energy uncertainty relation (Sec.4 note); it rests on two norm-positivity lemmas (App. A) and the kernel inequality S_m >= S~_m (App. B)

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (28 checks, exit 0; output saved to rederive/gr-qc_9607003.out). A: Lorentzian sampler has unit integral and Fourier transform e^{-|W| t0}, the step Eq.(7)+(8) -> Eq.(9). B: the V->oo mode sum -1/(2V) SUM w e^{-2 w t0} -> -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4) exactly = Eq.(17); Eq.(13) at m=0 agrees. C: G(0)=1, G strictly decreasing (massive bound tighter), substitution Eq.(13)->(14) exact. D: EM Eq.(48) = -3/(16 pi^2 t0^4) = 2 x scalar. E: 2D -1/(8 pi t0^2), F(y)->1. F: the App.B kernel e^{-|wi-wj|t0} - e^{-(wi+wj)t0} is PSD on 400 random spectra (min normalised eigenvalue +4.6e-5). G: END-TO-END on 21,900 (random multimode Bogoliubov/squeezed state, phase) pairs over box modes, Eq.(9) evaluated exactly never falls below the finite-V bound Eq.(12) restricted to the occupied modes (max (bound - rho_hat)/|bound| = -0.188); guard: 612 pairs have negative rho-hat, so the test is not vacuous; the single-mode squeezed vacuum approaches the finite-V bound to 0.998587 as e^{-2 w t0} -> 1 and never crosses it; control: a bound half as large IS violated. H: 3 hbar/(32 pi^2 c^3 t0^4) at t0 = L/c equals 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4); ford_roman(1 nm) = 3.00309e8; 105.276 = 32 pi^2/3 exactly. I: static <T00> gives rho-hat = rho0, so Eq.(1) for all t0 forces rho0 >= 0 in flat space. J: Fewster-Eveson (1/16 pi^2) INT (g'')^2 at g = sqrt(Lorentzian) = 27/(2048 pi^2 t0^4) = 9/64 of Ford-Roman (agrees with fewsterteo.py's 9/64 by a different route). L (added in the second session): Flanagan's optimal 2D bound at the Lorentzian is exactly 1/6 of Ford-Roman's 2D Eq.(25) and FE's 2D bound 1/4 of it (INT f'^2/f = 1/(2 t0^2)), both as FE p.8 prints; the Lorentzian tail is t^-2, outside FE's rapid-decay class. K: crossover 0.307933 l_P, shortfall 4.0371e52, crossover independent of G/hbar/c. NOT checked: Lemma A (App. A) was read, not machine-checked: a finite Fock truncation breaks [a,a+]=1, and the lemma is the norm identity (A3), which follows from the CCR in one line. The end-to-end check G exercises both lemmas implicitly.

later_literature.ref: Kontou & Sanders, 'Energy conditions in general relativity and quantum field theory', arXiv:2003.01815 (CQG 2020)
later_literature.what: p.21 restates the flat inertial massless/massive minimally coupled QWEI (61) for all Hadamard states and attributes the Lorentzian case to Ford-Roman [73,74]. For the Lorentzian it gives C = 3/(32 pi^2). Table 3: a state-independent QWEI holds for massless and massive minimally coupled KG, Maxwell/Proca, Dirac, 2D CFT and Ising, and is IMPOSSIBLE for xi != 0. p.4 and p.24: QEIs for interacting fields in general are 'less clear'. p.25: no null-worldline QEI in 4D (Fewster-Roman). DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT A REFUTATION (re-read p.21-22): p.21 writes (61) with the weight f^2 and says it 'was first derived by Ford and Roman [73,74] for Lorentzian functions f(t) = t0/(pi(t^2+t0^2))'; p.22 then says 'for a Lorentzian function, C = 3/(32 pi^2)'. Read literally with f^2 = Lorentzian (Ford-Roman's actual weight), (61) gives 27/(2048 pi^2) = 9/64 of that C (script J1; FE's own Eq.(5.6)). So the review's C is Ford-Roman's own constant, not the value of (61), and the phrasing is loose about f versus f^2. Not an error in gr-qc/9607003. p.34 also records that Casimir negative energy is constant in time and violates AWEC: consistent with H3 (Eq.(1) is for no boundaries).
later_literature.read_status: READ (pp.1,20-25,27,34 via answer_pdf_queries; re-read in the second session)

later_literature.ref: Fewster & Eveson, 'Bounds on negative energy densities in flat space-time', PRD 58, 084010 (1998), gr-qc/9805024
later_literature.what: Generalises Ford-Roman to smooth, even, non-negative samplers that are compactly supported or rapidly decaying, any dimension d >= 2, mass m >= 0 (abstract). 4D massless Eq.(5.5): rho >= -(1/16 pi^2) INT ((f^{1/2})'')^2 dt; at the Lorentzian Eq.(5.6) gives -27/(2048 pi^2 tau^4), 'which is 9/64 of Ford and Roman's result' (reproduced exactly here, script J1). In 4D the massless bound also bounds massive fields (Q_3 <= 1). In 2D their bound is 4x stronger than Ford-Roman at the Lorentzian and Flanagan's optimal one 6x (script L1, L2). This SHARPENS the bound (against M) and supports 'not saturated'. Stated limits (named, not hidden): a formal derivation 'lacking in mathematical rigour' (p.9); rapid decay required, which the Lorentzian (t^-2 tail) does not meet though FE apply (5.6) to it; state class 'sufficiently well-behaved', Hadamard hoped for. A sharp box (characteristic function) sampler gives NO bound (p.9, Garfinkle): consistent with the tree's no-ball-QI reading only for SHARP spacetime boxes, not a statement about smooth spatial averages.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested here: did the authors lack data that would change the conclusion? No, and the evidence runs one way. Eq.(1) is a theorem about the free massless minimally coupled scalar in 4D Minkowski space, and no measured quantity enters it (the constant is 3!/(2^4 4 pi^2)). The re-derivation here reproduces every step: the Fourier identity, both lemmas' consequence end to end on 21,900 state/phase pairs with a non-vacuity guard, the V -> oo limit, and the massive, EM and 2D companions. What the 1996 authors lacked was later THEORY, not data. (a) The general-sampler analysis (Fewster-Eveson 1998, READ; not itself optimal, per FE p.8-10) makes the Lorentzian bound 64/9 TIGHTER, which moves against M. (b) Proofs in curved spacetime (Fewster-Smith 2008, Kontou-Olum 2015) back the Sec.4 remark that was only 'argued' in 1996. (c) Knowledge of which hypotheses are load-bearing: non-minimal coupling admits NO state-independent QEI (Fewster-Osterbrink 2008), interacting 4D fields remain open, and there is no null-line QEI in 4D and no spatial-only QEI in 4D (Ford-Helfer-Roman, ledger D6). Point (c) is where the statement's REACH is narrower than a loose reading, and it is exactly where the tree's own L4 breaker (non-minimal coupling) sits. None of it moves the published conclusion within its stated hypotheses. The only numerical inputs the tree adds (hbar, c, G) are exact by definition or cancel from the tree's crossover (script K3).
grade_evidence: The published theorem STANDS. It was read at source, re-derived symbolically, and checked end to end on 21,900 squeezed-state/phase pairs (a non-vacuity guard and a control show the check can fail), and no datum it depends on has moved. The grade is NARROWED because of how the tree USES it, which is wider than the published class. (1) candidates.py:112-116, 346-348 and overturn.py:277 state it as '|rho| <= 3 hbar c/(32 pi^2 L^4)', dropping both the sampling (H4) and the one-sidedness (H5); the source says the pointwise density 'may be unboundedly negative' (p.2). (2) overturn.py:220-222 says it bounds |rho| 'over a sampling region rather than an average along a line', which contradicts p.4's single spatial point x = 0 on an inertial worldline. (3) candidates.py:363-364 puts a spatial corridor size R into the temporal width t0 (L = c t0 = R), a choice the source does not make. The tree's own DOCKET 55 already withdraws this for achievable.py and not for candidates.py or overturn.py. (4) The Sec.4 curved-spacetime scope, carried in noise.py and the split key, is in this paper an ARGUED claim (ref.[23]) with two worked cases (Casimir plates, static RW), and noise.py drops 'and/or the distance to any boundaries'. Later literature proves versions of it for the minimally coupled free scalar (Fewster-Smith 2008, Kontou-Olum 2015, via Kontou-Sanders). The tree's usage errs AGAINST M, not for M, in two places: flat-space Eq.(1) for all t0 excludes a static negative density outright (script I1/I2), which is stronger than the tree's L = R cut; and Fewster-Eveson's bound is 9/64 of Ford-Roman's (script J1). FE's own Eq.(5.6) (READ) prints that 9/64; it supports, but because the Lorentzian sits outside FE's stated rapid-decay class and FE's derivation is self-described as formal it does not prove, that Ford-Roman's 4D Lorentzian constant is never attained (in 2D Flanagan's optimal bound makes it firm, script L1). That supports the tree's own record that bounds.py's K = 0 ('known saturated') coding is wrong. That is a fault in the tree, not in the source. No WRONG: nothing in gr-qc/9607003 is refuted, and no misprint was found (the text layer's 't0' for the proper-time coordinate on p.2 is an extraction artefact, and p.4 has 't'). Second session: source, Kontou-Sanders and Fewster-Eveson re-read at alphaXiv; the script re-run (28 checks, all pass); every owner file:line quoted above was re-checked against the tree read-only.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: every owner restates the result as a one-sided lower bound on the Lorentzian time-average along an inertial worldline at one spatial point (as certify.py and bounds.py:234 already do), and candidates.py's L = R step is carried as a named modelling hypothesis whose authority is the Sec.4 argued extension (or Kontou-Olum's proved small-curvature QWEI), not Eq.(1). To WRONG (for the source): an explicit Fock state of the free massless minimally coupled scalar in 4D Minkowski with rho-hat < -3/(32 pi^2 t0^4). None was found on 21,900 random squeezed-state/phase pairs, and Fewster-Eveson's 9/64-tighter bound would forbid it. To OPEN: none, since the source is read and the derivation is closed-form. Separately, the support for 'Ford-Roman 4D is not saturated' (and so for the tree's K = 0 WRONG record) would fall if FE's Eq.(5.6) were shown invalid for the Lorentzian sampler, which lies outside FE's stated rapid-decay class; it would not change this grade, which rests on the tree's usage.
